                           THE REPORT OF AN UNIDENTIFIED MOVING OBJECT OR OBJECTS AS
                           SEEN IN THE .SKY AT NIGHT TIME BY R. GRANDY IRWIN ON THE
                           DATES AS LISTED FRO~! THE OBSERVATION POINT OF THE WESTERN
                           VERANDA OF HIS RESIDENCE IN SHELBURNE AT THE CORNER OF 1
                           WATER STREET AND ST. PATRICKS LANE .
                                   ,
                                                                                                                                                      ·-
                           August• 12tb       9 . ~5   P, M.
                                   While witnessing the depar~ure o~ twilight from the
                           vantage point 1of mr veranda steps on the WesUern side of my
                           residence in Shel burne at the Corner of Water Street and
                           St . Patricka. Lane and while observing the appearance of night-
                           fall and the appearance of the first stars of the night I
                           observed the first star to appear to my vision was the Evening
·.                         Star in a direction slightly North of West and at an angle of
                           approximately 40 degrees above the horizon .     I also observed
                           a lesser star at an angle of approximately JS degrees above the
                           horizon and about 5 degrees to the right of the1Evening Star.
                                     Suddenly a light appeared between the two stars men-
                           tioned.       It had the appearance of being another star and
                           was fully , as bright as the Evenin~ Star and it was in motion
                        , at the precise time of its appearance and it quickly ' gave the
     •                     appearance of passing between th~ two stars already mentioned
                           and it proceeded in a South Westerly direction. \ There was no
                           sound and the night was calm. The object left no vapor trail
                         · or 'other residue to mark its progress .      I call to my wife
                           who wae home at the time ~o come and witness this unusual sight
                           but she was watching television and did not hear me call and
                           I was regretfully compelled to witness this happening alone .
                                •.    The o.bject was pnoceeding at an enormous speed and      ,
                           veere9 first to the' left and then to the right at very sharp angles
                           of approximately ~5 degrees at each change of direction. These
                           changes of direction were instantaneous and required no dis-
                           ~ernable lapse of time .     It appeared to change direction about
                           six times ' but always remained on its general course toward
                           the South West , where i~ d~sappe~red . frQm my vision . Whether      '
                           its disappearance waa by reason bf the great distan~e_ it had
                           travel led or whether the light had been extin~is~ed by ~echanical
                           meantlr it ia impossible for me to say. - THT ell.~psed t[ille from
                           the t~~ of sighting until the time· of its dts~pearan9e , I
                           woul d carefully estimate to have been ten se~o~ds .     I
